caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
data_source: IMF World Economic Outlook via DataMapper (latest vintage, accessed October 2026)
debt_management: Liechtenstein effectively has no public debt: 0.4% of GDP in 2006, peaking at 0.6% in 2017 (the series high), and a projected 0.5% in 2025 — rounding error in any framework. The state runs structural surpluses on financial-services and manufacturing revenues, and the fiscal rule limits spending growth. GDP grew from $4.4bn in 2006 to a projected $9.0bn in 2025. Debt sustainability is a non-question; the fiscal debate is about reserves and intergenerational funds.
inflation_management: Liechtenstein uses the Swiss franc in a customs and monetary union with Switzerland, so it imports Swiss monetary policy entirely. Inflation tracked Switzerland's: -0.5% in 2009, -1.1% in 2015 (the low) after the franc's appreciation, -0.7% in 2020, then just 2.8% in 2022 (the series high) — barely a ripple compared with the euro area's energy shock. It was 1.1% in 2024 and is projected at 0.2% for 2025. The franc's safe-haven strength is the perennial competitiveness question, not price stability.

key_events.event: Banking-secrecy era ended: tax-information agreements and OECD compliance reforms transformed the financial center.
Swiss franc shock (January 2015): the SNB's cap removal appreciated the franc; Liechtenstein absorbed it with -1.1% inflation.
COVID-19: the economy contracted but the fiscal position never came under pressure.
Energy shock produced only 2.8% inflation, the series high, on franc strength and Swiss policy.

outlook_next_decade: Liechtenstein's outlook is one of stability: no debt, price stability imported from Switzerland, and a high-value industrial and financial base. The structural risks are regulatory — EU and OECD pressure on financial centers — and the franc's chronic strength squeezing exporters. Neither threatens the macro position. The analytical assessment is straightforward: this is one of the world's most fiscally secure economies, with limited upside or downside on the macro side.
